newsDocuments.headline: Oil prices near three-month lows as rising supply offsets Hormuz threat

segments.text: SINGAPORE: Oil prices extended their falls into a second day on Tuesday to trade near three-month lows on signs of rising crude supply and a potential market surplus, though risks to shipping through the Strait of Hormuz persisted.
Brent crude futures fell 66 cents, or 0.7%, to $88.71 a barrel by 0510 GMT, after posting their lowest close since August 31 on Monday.
US West Texas Intermediate crude futures slipped 60 cents, or 0.8%, to $79.57 a barrel, after hitting their lowest level since August 26 earlier in the session.

newsDocuments.headline: Palm extends losses on weaker rivals, crude oil

segments.text: JAKARTA: Malaysian palm oil futures dropped for a sixth straight session on Tuesday to trade near their lowest level in about nine months, weighed down by weakness in Dalian and Chicago rivals, while lower crude oil prices also added pressu
The benchmark palm oil contract for February delivery on the Bursa Malaysia Derivatives Exchange declined 30 ringgit, or 0.72%, to 4,111 ringgit ($997.82) a metric ton by the midday break.

“Bursa Malaysia crude palm oil futures opened lower, tracking spread with Dalian RBD palm olein futures. Continued weakness in rival oilseeds may limit further recovery and keep market sentiment subdued,” a Kuala Lumpur-based trader said.

newsDocuments.headline: Oil, gas exploration, production companies: Panel flags incomplete production data to DGPC (PD)

segments.text: ISLAMABAD: A parliamentary panel on Monday expressed serious concerns that certain oil and gas exploration and production companies, including Pakistan Exploration Limited (PEL), have not been providing complete production-related informati

The sub-committee of the Senate Standing Committee on Petroleum, under convenorship of Senator Jam Saifullah Khan Dharejo, held a meeting at the Sui Southern Gas Company (SSGC), Karachi. The committee released a handout after the meeting.
The Committee also examined the status of petroleum exploration and production licences, particularly those issued over extended periods.

newsDocuments.headline: Oil drops more than 3pc on increased ME flows

segments.text: HOUSTON: Oil prices shed more than 3 percent on Monday as traders weighed a rise in supplies from the Middle East and the restart of a Libyan oil pipeline, offsetting some unease around shipping and refinery attacks in the region.
Brent crude futures fell USD3.25, or 3.51 percent, to USD89.32 a barrel by 12:02 p.m. EDT. US West Texas Intermediate futures were down USD2.97, or 3.56 percent, at USD80.44 a barrel.
Earlier in the session, Brent hit a session low of USD88.60 a barrel, its lowest since August 27, while WTI fell to a low of USD79.95, its lowest since August 26.
